4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your Block Breaker game, published, where bricks disappear when the ball hits them, plus your game link and one sentence about your rule on your portfolio site.
4th Period.workingNow: Telling Copilot the trigger and the change, so a brick disappears when the ball touches it.
4th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can write a Copilot prompt with a trigger (the ball touches a brick) and a change (that brick disappears) and see a brick vanish, so my game has its first new feature.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including nested loops and compound conditionals.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas and information, using appropriate technology.
agenda: I do and we do: write the Copilot prompt (13 min)
You do: make a brick disappear (17 min)
Exit Ticket: your trigger and change (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you found the code where the ball bounces off a brick. Today you tell Copilot what should happen when the ball touches one: the trigger is the touch and the change is the brick disappearing. Tomorrow you play your game, find one problem, and fix it.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: one photo of the lever you built, with the fulcrum, load, and effort labeled.
6th Period.workingNow: Learning the 6 simple machines, then building a lever together as a class.

We do: build the class lever (22 min)

6th Period.connections: Yesterday you found things in our room that make a job easier. Today you learn those are simple machines, and there are six. We build one lever together and name its parts. Tomorrow you build your own.
